title: design-map visual vocabulary and agent preview
requirement: The owner asked for the design map to be convenient for the agent — the agent must explicitly understand the visual representation it produces — and maximally convenient for the human to read and edit: a deliberate visual vocabulary (node kinds, layers, title, labelled flows) that the agent can reason about, a preview and health verdict in every tool result, and every label still editable in the real editor.
reason: Intake requirement recorded from chat before implementation; the observed proof is reports/design-map-v2/cases.mjs (53 assertions) and the screens under reports/design-map-v2/screens, not a case-library automated test.
steps: Ask the orchestrator to write a design map with layers, kinds, a title and labelled flows.
Open the Design map panel and confirm the shapes, bands, title and arrow labels are visible.
Double-click a box and an arrow and edit their text.
Drag a box, then ask the orchestrator for an unrelated upsert; the dragged box and its band must not move.
Read the tool result: it must contain preview and health.
expected: A design_map write/upsert can declare kind (service/store/decision/external -> rectangle/ellipse/diamond/dashed rectangle), layer + layers[] (titled bands), a title, and edge labels; the scene shows all of them in the real Excalidraw frame; every result returns a text preview of the real geometry and a health verdict; double-clicking a shape or an arrow edits its label; an upsert never moves a box or band the human placed.
